text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- In the year 2003 the value of EU funds transferred to Portugal may fall to one third of the present value due to the enlargenment of the European Union and a refusal by the richer countries to boost their contributions.

- State energy company Petrogal is worth 50 billion escudos more due to the recent discovery of an oil field off Angola. Petrogal has a participation of nine percent on the group of companies that are exploring the field.

- National olive oil production does not cover half domestic demand. To increase the production, the Governemnt announced a plan for the the next 20 years that includes restructuring and planting of new olive groves as well as modernising the industry.

- The number of people unemployed and under-employed rose to 14.4 percent of Portugal's active population in the first quarter of 1997, according to the National Statistics Institute. This number contradicts government's forecasts for a fall.

- The biggest investments under the European Programme for the Development of Portuguese Industry (PEDIP II) were made in the production of electronic components, followed by audio-visual material and financial activities.
- The Financial Markets Committee (CMVM) is studying the application of a directive that obliges members of the European Union to constitute a guarantee fund for investors.

- Assets of non-real estate investment funds grew 1.7 percent to 3.02 trillion escudos in March, below the five percent per month rates of growth seen in recent months. Year-on-year, the total was up 35 percent.
